evidences.evidence_quote: The tranditional method is difﬁcult to achieve satisﬁed results due to the imprecise estimation of the static component. Therefore, TagVibra takes advantage of the modulation scheme of RFID and proposes a phase ampliﬁcation algorithm (Differential Phase Ampliﬁcation, DPA) to eliminate the impact of static component and amplify the phase change. The basic idea of DPA is behind Equ.5, which can be rewritten as: { V1 =Vs +V1 tag V0 =Vs +V0 tag (6) Since V1 and V0 both contain the same static component Vs, an intuitive method is to eliminate the impact of the static component by making a difference betweenV1 and V0. However, the resulting phase change may be very slight (since the angular changes ofV1 and V0 should be identical when the static component is eliminated, in theory). To solve this problem, we calculated the average value ofV0 (regard asV0) and subtract it from V1. Since V0 contains the same static component asV1, the impact of the static component can still be eliminated after subtraction. sinceV0 is a point, the phase change ofV1 −V0 can be measured directly. Even better, since V0 is closer toV1 than the distance between the origin andV1, the phase change ofV1 can be effectively ampliﬁed: ΔV =V1 −V0 =V1 tag −V0 tag (7) Compared toV0 or V1, we have eliminated the static component, and ΔV only retains tag’s reﬂection signals related to vibration. Therefore, as shown in Fig. 6(b), compared to the raw phase, the modulated phase is signiﬁcantly ampliﬁed.
evidences.evidence_context: The paragraph describes the DPA algorithm proposed by TagVibra. The citation [17] appears only at the end of the previous sentence: 'RFID tag modulates its data on the backscatter signal using ON-OFF keying scheme. We regard them asVi tag, wherei=0 or 1 represents the matching and mismatching states of the antenna impedance of the tag, respectively [16] [17].' The citation [17] is grouped with [16] and points to the background knowledge of tag modulation, not to the sub-mm or through-wall claim.
